messages:
Maya: Heads-up — customer 'Acme' opened an escalation: p99 for /v1/generate jumped from ~140ms to ~2s around 2026-03-15T15:12Z. They attached slow traces and said it's not auth/billing.

Liam: Thanks. Any infra deploys or config flips near that time? Which clusters?

ops-bot: deploy: runtime-cluster-prod-5 updated at 2026-03-15T15:05 by arjun -> runtime:2026.03.15-rc5 (cache-serializer tweak).

Arjun: I pushed a tiny change to the cache key serializer to include extra metadata for debugging. I thought we excluded runtime-only fields, but I may have left traceId in there.

Noah: Observing high cache cardinality on nodes in pool-5 starting ~15:06. Keys look unique per-request. Eviction rate jumped and GC pressure rose.

Maya: Graph snippets: cache.hit_ratio.prod.pool5 fell from 0.91 -> 0.47 in ~10m; evictions spiked to 5k/min; kv.backend p99 climbed 320ms -> 1.1s.

Emma (support): Customer provided this trace: 
```
[15:13:08] runtime: cache.get(key=hash:fe12...) -> MISS
[15:13:09] runtime: remote-kv.fetch(prefix=prompt+trace:d3f...) -> 390ms
[15:13:09] runtime: respond -> 2.04s
```

Liam: If traceId got into the key, every request becomes effectively unique -> total cache churn and no prefix reuse. That explains p99 tail and backend saturation.

Arjun: Confirmed. Patch diff:
```
- key = stableHash({prompt, model, user, traceId})
+ key = stableHash({prompt, model, user})  // traceId should be omitted
```
I can revert immediately.

Noah: We're also seeing eviction loop contend with token-generator threads. Eviction thrashing causing CPU spikes and some slow GC cycles.

Liam: Immediate actions: 1) revert the serializer change and push hotfix; 2) increase in-memory cache capacity by 25% on affected pools; 3) sequentially restart the worst nodes to reclaim memory; 4) prepare a warmup job to prefill hot prefixes for the customer. If needed, throttle that customer's rate briefly.

Arjun: Reverted and pushed runtime:2026.03.15-hotfix. Deploy started. deploy-bot shows rollout to prod-5 (rolling update).

deploy-bot: rollout: runtime:2026.03.15-hotfix -> prod-5 (4/20 pods updated)

Maya: Making the emergency capacity bump now on pools 5/6. Noah, please restart nodes one-by-one and watch hit ratio and GC.

Noah: Restarting node-45 now (15:24). Holding for 2m.

Noah: node-45 back. Hit ratio on node-45 improved from 0.48 -> 0.79. Evictions down on that node.

Maya: Early recovery signals: global hit ratio up to 0.72 by 15:32, kv backend p99 back to ~140ms by 15:36. Customer still seeing a few spikes at 15:34-15:37.

Liam: Those residual spikes likely because cold keys need warmup. Arjun, can you run a one-off prefill of top prefixes used by Acme? Use their top-100 prefixes from the hot-keys index and populate local caches.

Arjun: Doing that now. Warmup script queued and running against pool-5 memstores. It will sequentially read keys then prime local cache.

Maya: Also added temporary alert: if cache.hit_ratio drops >20% in 10m and evictions >1000/min, page eng-sre.

cs-bot: ticket-#4321 updated: Engineering deploying hotfix + warmup; monitoring.

Emma (support): Customer updated at 15:38: "Saw initial improvement, still occasional tails but much better overall. Awaiting final confirmation."

Noah: Note: we saw a pattern where TTLs were set to 7d for these keys, so the serializer bug created long-lived unique entries that filled memory. We should avoid long TTLs for keys that include high-cardinality fields.

Liam: Agreed. Post-incident actions: 1) enforce stable key schema that explicitly excludes ephemeral fields; 2) add unit/integration test to assert low-cardinality key cardinality for representative traffic; 3) change eviction policy to cost-aware LRU so large entries or low-QPS entries are deprioritized; 4) add pre-deploy canary that looks at key cardinality delta.

Arjun: I pushed a permanent fix in main that removes traceId and includes a serializer blacklist for ephemeral fields. Added tests that run locally. Will open PR for service-level predeploy check.

Liam: Incident created INC-20260315-1792 for tracking. Pager duty notified.

Maya: Customer confirmed at 15:46 that p99 returned to baseline. We'll leave monitoring on and keep warmup for 2 hours. Closing message to CS sent.

Noah: I'll follow up with a staging chaos test that injects high-cardinality keys into cache serializer to ensure alerting triggers early.

Liam: Thanks all. Saved dashboards and flamegraphs to the incident ticket. Add any remaining follow-ups to the ticket. :thumbsup:
